result.title: Fewer Tokens, Better Action: GPT-6 Astra Robot Agents with 14% Higher Success Rate but 65% Fewer Tokens
result.summary: Vision language model (VLM) agents can control robots through visual feedback and action primitives, but repeated model invocations and redundant observations incur substantial token overhead. We introduce PyRUA-Lean, an interactive code-execution framework that couples feedback-driven primitive composition with selective observation: the agent composes classical robot primitives and learned vision-language-action (VLA) policies into Python cells that perform conditional checks and local retries, returning only explicitly requested images and state feedback for replanning. Across 700 simulated task instances from LIBERO-PRO, RoboTwin 2.0, and RoboCasa365, we compare PyRUA-Lean with a tool-calling baseline using the same GPT-6 Astra planner and underlying robot primitives. Under equal LLM-call budgets, PyRUA-Lean increases overall success from 63.1% to 71.7%. On instances solved by both agents, it uses 49% fewer LLM calls and 65% fewer input tokens.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作提出 PyRUA-Lean：通过代码执行把经典机器人原语与学习型 VLA 策略组合成带条件判断和局部重试的 Python 单元，并只返回显式请求的图像与状态，从而在多个仿真基准上减少 LLM 调用与输入 token 的同时提升成功率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「选择性观察 + 条件重试」构成了一种显式的获取证据与停止/重规划决策机制，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的成本权衡与视觉证据筛选提供参照，但原文未涉及 latent 状态，相关性需核查其 token 节省是否来自观测裁剪而非推理状态压缩。
